items.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care. METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1 . Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants’ effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case–control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed. RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case–control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants. CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.
items.limitations: One limitation of our study is the inability to capture splice variants, which can be addressed using complementary high-throughput splicing assays or endogenous gene editing approaches. Additionally, because KCNE1 co-expression occludes labeling of the KCNQ1 myc tag and prevents binding of the KCNQ1 activator compounds, we did not incorporate KCNE1 into our MAVE abundance or function assays. This could potentially lead to discordant results in some variant pathogenicity classifications, although it has been shown that coexpression of KCNQ1 with KCNE1 generally results in only mild changes in KCNQ1 cell surface abundance. The MAVE experiments were performed in HEK293 cells that may not express the full suite of KCNQ1-interacting or regulating proteins. We also did not model certain features of KCNQ1 biology, such as adrenergic stimulation.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
items.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

items.title: Mainstreaming Cardiovascular Care for Women: From Special Population to Standard Practice

A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

items.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages—perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)—to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

items.title: One Life Course, Many Specialties: Building a System for Cardiovascular Health in Girls and Women
items.abstract: ardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women and men, yet women remain underrepresented in clinical trials, remain undertreated, and often experience worse outcomes.Their hormonal, physiological, psychosocial, and therapeutic risks require tailored care.The 3 multispecialty publications in this issue of Circulation describe women's cardiovascular life course, guide prevention and management, and examine women's cardiovascular disease centers.Together, they establish a scientific foundation for reorganizing care around women throughout their lives.

items.title: Women’s Cardiovascular Health: From Recognition to Action
Promises to Keep: Closing the Gaps in Women’s Cardiovascular Health
Women’s Cardiovascular Health Begins in Childhood

Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
items.abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women’s cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women’s cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.

Price Variation in Outpatient Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
items.abstract: ore than 600 000 percutaneous coronary interventions (PCIs) are performed annually in the United States. 1 Increasing procedural safety, same-day discharge pathways, and expansion of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement have accelerated the transition of elective PCI into outpatient settings, including hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs).[2][3][4] Although outpatient PCI may reduce resource utilization and overall spending, little is known about how negotiated prices vary across outpatient sites of care. 2 The 2021 Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to disclose payer-specific negotiated rates for all services and has enabled national analyses of pricing variation for cardiovascular services.5 Previous work leveraging these data has demonstrated substantial variation in commercial prices for common cardiovascular procedures, but outpatient PCI pricing remains poorly characterized.5 We used national price transparency data to quantify variation in prices for outpatient PCI across HOPDs versus ASCs and to evaluate associations between facility characteristics and negotiated commercial prices.

items.title: Optimizing US Prehospital Care of ST-Segment–Elevation Myocardial Infarction Because Time Is Life, Not Just Muscle
items.abstract: Time is muscle" in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is the foundational principle of STEMI care, but even more importantly, time is also life since mortality rises rapidly with delays beyond the "golden hour." 1 With the steep decline in in-hospital mortality for STEMI, the majority of deaths due to STEMI now occur out-ofhospital.Thus, the greatest opportunity for improving STEMI outcomes lies in reducing the interval between symptom onset and reperfusion of the thrombolytic occlusion, which can be achieved in some patients with a glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor or a thrombolytic agent, and in nearly all patients with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).Herein, we provide five recommendations for reducing this critical time interval, ranging from patient education to pre-hospital pharmaceuticals to changes in reimbursement for pre-hospital care teams (Figure 1).

items.title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials
items.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

items.title: Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy Demonstrated by Coronary Angiography and Histopathological Correlates
Care Pathways to Support People Living With Heart Failure
ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis. METHODS: ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2 -modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity. RESULTS: In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF. CONCLUSIONS: In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

items.title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS ( P =0.784). CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

items.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14–0.66]; P =0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06–0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04864145

items.title: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in US Veterans
Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples
items.abstract: Background: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment. Methods: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF. Results: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040). Conclusions: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

items.abstract: coronary heart disease ◼ ezetimibe ◼ hypolipidemic agents ◼ low-density lipoprotein ◼ statins W hile the breadth of Dr Eugene Braunwald's contributions to cardiology is staggering, few lines of inquiry rival the relentless perseverance with which he pushed forward the field of lipid lowering in what he termed "the race to the bottom." 1 Dr Braunwald described his first exposure to the lipid hypothesis of atherogenesis in the 1950s while at the National Heart Institute (now the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute), through interactions with a biochemist and future Nobel Laureate, Christian B. Anfinsen. 1 Dr Braunwald noted that while the lipid hypothesis had not yet gained widespread acceptance, these interactions left him convinced of the validity of the hypothesis and, consequently, the role for treatment of hyperlipidemia in patients with atherosclerosis.At the time, Dr Braunwald's research efforts continued to focus on reducing myocardial infarct size, but he resolved to revisit treatment of hyperlipidemia in the future when better therapies became available.

Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B. METHODS: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis. RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P =0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P =0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P <0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P =0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P <0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P <0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04153149.

items.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined. METHODS: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats. RESULTS: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models. CONCLUSIONS: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA’s catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

items.title: 2026 International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations: Summary from the Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid Task Forces
items.abstract: This is the annual summary of the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Consensus on Science With Treatment Recommendations ; a comprehensive review was completed in 2025. This latest summary addresses the most recent published resuscitation evidence reviewed by International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation task forces, including Basic Life Support; Advanced Life Support; Pediatric Life Support; Neonatal Life Support; Education, Implementation, and Teams; and First Aid. Members from these 6 task forces assessed the certainty of the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation criteria, and their statements include consensus treatment recommendations. Highlights from task force discussions and insights into how decisions regarding treatment recommendations were made are provided in the Justification and Evidence-to-Decision Framework Highlights sections. The task forces also listed priority knowledge gaps for further research.

Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions
items.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
items.abstract: Background Current guidelines recommend echocardiographic surveillance every 1-2 years for patients with moderate aortic stenosis (AS). Ongoing randomized trials are evaluating transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for patients with moderate AS and at-risk features associated with rapid progression or poor outcomes. The prevalence and prognostic impact of these features in clinical practice are unknown. Objectives To determine the prevalence and prognostic impact of at-risk features in real-world clinical practice among patients with moderate AS. Methods We analyzed deidentified data from 14,859,523 patients at 48 US institutions (egnite Registry; IRB exempt). Patients with moderate or severe AS per echocardiographic assessment (ACC/AHA guidelines) identified on or after January 1 , 2022, were included. At-risk features for moderate AS (PROGRESS trial criteria) included valve-related symptoms, left ventricular ejection fraction <60%, diastolic dysfunction grade ≥2, stroke volume index <35 mL/m , atrial fibrillation, or elevated natriuretic peptide. Outcomes were 2-year mortality, hospitalization with heart failure, aortic valve replacement (AVR), and progression to severe AS (Kaplan-Meier for mortality; Aalen-Johansen with death as a competing event for the others). Results Among 53,994 patients with at least moderate AS, 35,343 (65.5%) were moderate, and 18,651 (34.5%) were severe. Among patients with moderate AS, 27,815 (78.7%) had at least 1 at-risk feature. At 2 years, the cumulative mortality for patients with moderate AS without at-risk features, moderate AS with at-risk features, and severe AS was 9.0% (95% CI, 8.1–9.9), 20.1% (95% CI, 19.5–20.7), and 23.5% (95% CI, 22.7–24.3), and hospitalization with heart failure was 21.9% (95% CI, 20.7–23.2), 44.6% (95% CI, 43.8–45.3), and 54.8% (95% CI, 53.9–55.8), respectively (p value <0.0001 for both). With follow-up censored at AVR, progression to severe AS at 2 years was similar with and without at-risk features (28.2% vs 26.3%). Conclusions In this large real-world cohort, the vast majority of patients with moderate AS had at-risk features and experienced worse clinical outcomes, with 2-fold higher risks of mortality and hospitalization with heart failure than those without at-risk features, despite similar progression to severe AS. These findings support risk-based stratification of moderate AS and investigation of strategies to reduce adverse events in patients with at-risk features.

Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications. METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications. RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%). CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

items.abstract: Background Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown. Objectives This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy. Results A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients Conclusions This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes
items.abstract: Background Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear. Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR). Methods This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11). Conclusions recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

items.title: Dynamic Common Iliac Vein Compression by the Adjacent Intestine Revealed by Intravascular Ultrasound
Morphology-Dependent Dose-Response of Intravascular Lithotripsy on Coronary Calcium Fracture
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves to modify calcification to enable optimal balloon and stent expansion in calcified lesions. However, the dose-response relationship for creating fractures within calcified lesions of different calcium morphologies is unknown. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of IVL on calcium fracture overall and in the setting of calcification arc <180° vs ≥180°. METHODS: Micro-computed tomography images were acquired before and after 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 120 pulses of IVL treatment (Shockwave Medical) in an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric human hearts (15 coronary lesions). A total of 30 cross-sections of micro-computed tomography (2 sections per lesion) were analyzed for this study. RESULTS: Cumulative fracture occurrence increased progressively with the number of IVL pulses delivered, with fractures observed in 33% of sections after 10 pulses, 50% after 40 pulses, and 60% after 120 pulses. Calcification arc ≥180° exhibited a higher fracture occurrence compared with arc <180° (P = 0.028). After adjustment for pulse number, calcification arc ≥180° was associated with significantly higher fracture counts compared with arc <180° (rate ratio = 6.1, P = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Fracture occurrence following IVL increased with cumulative pulse delivery and differed significantly according to calcification concentricity. Calcification arc ≥180° demonstrated a higher and earlier likelihood of fracture occurrence than arc <180°, independent of pulse number. These findings establish a clear dose-dependent relationship between IVL pulse delivery and fracture formation and highlight calcification concentricity as a key determinant of fracture response.

Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI
items.abstract: Background Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. Objectives The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. Methods This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P Conclusions Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

items.title: Calcium Fracture Detection by Optical Coherence Tomography Versus Intravascular Ultrasound Following Intravascular Lithotripsy
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. We have shown previously that optical coherence tomography (OCT) misses approximately half of these fractures. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality. The sensitivity of IVUS for detecting calcium fractures after intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture observed on IVUS in comparison to OCT and gold standard micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) using heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels. METHODS: In an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric hearts (15 coronary lesions), OCT, IVUS, and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL coronary artery treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability. RESULTS: Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, but OCT demonstrated higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; fracture width >115 μm on OCT were identified by IVUS with excellent diagnostic performance (area under the curve: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-1.00], sensitivity 100%, specificity 92%). CONCLUSIONS: OCT and IVUS underestimate the occurrence of IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, with IVUS demonstrating lower sensitivity than OCT. IVUS detectability is strongly dependent on fracture width. Absence of visible fracture on either OCT or IVUS does not exclude calcium modification.

items.title: Beyond Procedural Success
Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair
items.abstract: Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Methods The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Results No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P 50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH. Conclusions Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

items.title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium
items.abstract: ObjectivesThis study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. MethodsFRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed. ResultsA total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). ConclusionsThe quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation. Registration: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240)

Paradoxical 1-Year Improvement in Right Ventricular Function After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement
Sirolimus- Versus Everolimus-Eluting Stents With Contemporary PCI in Three-Vessel Disease: The Multivessel TALENT Randomized Noninferiority Trial
items.abstract: Background Contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has improved outcomes in three-vessel disease (3VD). However, the Supraflex Cruz sirolimus-eluting stent (SES) has not been compared with the SYNERGY everolimus-eluting stent (EES) in this setting. Objectives We compared the performance of the Supraflex Cruz SES and the SYNERGY EES in patients with de novo 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI. Methods We randomized 1,548 patients to the Supraflex Cruz SES (n=774) or the SYNERGY EES (n=774). Patients were selected after Heart Team discussion incorporating the SYNTAX Score II. Contemporary PCI included angiography-derived physiology, intravascular imaging optimization, CTO expertise, and short DAPT followed by prasugrel monotherapy. The primary endpoint was the 1-year patient-oriented composite endpoint (POCE: all-cause death, any stroke, any myocardial infarction, or any revascularization), estimated by Kaplan–Meier in the intention-to-treat population. The non-inferiority margin was 4.28%. Results Median follow-up was 367 days (IQR, 362–372). At 1 year, POCE was 15.23% (95% CI, 12.87–17.96) with Supraflex Cruz SES and 14.51% (95% CI, 12.20–17.21) with SYNERGY EES. The risk difference was 0.72 percentage points; the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound was 3.71%, below the margin (P non-inferiority=0.025). Myocardial infarction occurred in 10.07% (95% CI, 8.14–12.43) versus 8.14% (95% CI, 6.41–10.33), revascularization in 6.40% (95% CI, 4.86–8.40) versus 6.81% (95% CI, 5.22–8.87), and stent thrombosis in 1.31% (95% CI, 0.71–2.43) versus 1.08% (95% CI, 0.54–2.14). Conclusions In patients with 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI, the Supraflex Cruz SES was noninferior to the SYNERGY EES for 1-year POCE. Clinical Trial Registration NCT04390672

items.title: Fully Retrievable Self-Expanding Short-Frame Valve for Aortic Regurgitation
Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement
items.abstract: Background Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants. Methods TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection. Results Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P 2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88). Conclusions Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

items.title: One Lesion, Two Perspectives
Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve and Valve-in-Ring Implantation: the TRIVIR registry
items.abstract: Background Transcatheter tricuspid valve-in-valve (TViV) and valve-in-ring (TViR) procedures are increasingly used; however, data on clinical outcomes, valve performance, and symptomatic improvement remain limited. Objectives To evaluate a real-world multicenter cohort undergoing transcatheter TViV and TViR procedures. Methods We conducted an international multicenter registry including patients undergoing TViV/TViR procedures. The TRIVIR Registry evaluated all-cause mortality and a composite endpoint (CE), defined as all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration during follow-up. Results Between 2012 and 2025, 75 patients underwent TViV (n=62) or TViR (n=13) across 16 centers using Sapien (88%) or Myval (12%) valves. Median follow up was 1.86 years (IQR 0.10-2.59). Mean age was 62±13 years, and 69% were women. NYHA class III–IV decreased from 72% at baseline to 13% at 1-3 months and remained low during follow-up. No 30-day deaths occurred, while periprocedural complications occurred in 24% of procedures, mostly minor (17.3%). At 3 years, the Kaplan–Meier estimates of all-cause mortality and CE were 35.6% and 42.9%, and the cumulative incidences of HF hospitalization and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration were 16.6% and 11.4%, respectively. Patients who died had markers of advanced disease, including higher NT-proBNP levels, greater diuretic requirements, more frequent pacing/CRT implantation, and higher procedural complication rates. Conclusions TViV/TViR represents a viable treatment strategy and provided sustained symptomatic improvement in high-risk patients. Patients who died exhibited a more advanced clinical profile, highlighting the importance of appropriate patient selection, early referral, and treatment in experienced centers.

items.title: Renal Outcomes With Staged Versus Concomitant PCI and TAVR
Extrinsic Left Main Coronary Compression Caused by Delayed Periaortic Hematoma After Aortic Valve Replacement

Thirty-Day Outcomes of a Dedicated Transcatheter Occlusion Device for Paravalvular Leak Closure: The PARADIGM Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a complication of surgical valve replacement and is associated with poor prognosis. Percutaneous device closure offers a less invasive alternative to repeat surgery. OBJECTIVE Evaluate the Amplatzer Valvular Plug III (APVL3) for PVL closure after surgical implant of a mechanical or bioprosthetic valve. METHODS PARADIGM is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study assessing transcatheter PVL closure. The primary endpoint was a composite of safety and effectiveness measures evaluating the implant success, PVL reduction ≥2 grades on exit from the procedure, procedural mortality, and device-related reinterventions through 30 days. Descriptive safety and performance endpoints were evaluated at 30 days. RESULTS A total of 200 patients were enrolled across 24 sites in the United States, Europe, and Canada. Average age was 67.7+/-11.5 years, 58.5% were male, and 70.0% had a mechanical valve. Median(IQR) logistic EuroSCORE was 5.2(3.2,10.3), median(IQR) STS PROM was 2.9%(1.4,5.4), and 53.1%(104/196) were NYHA class III/IV. Heart failure was the primary indication for PVL closure (89.5%), and 65.0% were treated for mitral PVL. Successful implantation was achieved in 96.0%(192/200), with no procedural mortality. The primary endpoint was met in 94.0%(188/200), exceeding the performance goal(P<0.0001). The 30-day procedural success was 77.3%(140/181). At 30 days, mortality was 2.0%(4/200,95%CI:0.5-5.0), hemolytic anemia occurred in 3.5%(7/200,95% CI:1.42%,7.08%), 95.7%(156/163) had mild or less PVL, 82.7%(143/173) were NYHA class I/II, and KCCQ-OS improved by 15.7(12.6,18.8) points. CONCLUSION PARADIGM met its primary endpoint, with favorable short-term outcomes. The results support this transcatheter device as a promising therapeutic option for PVL closure. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04489823

items.title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc). METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes. RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%). CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

items.title: TECTONIC CAD
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S. CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion. RESULTS: , with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting. CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

items.title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules
items.abstract: Background Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain. Objectives This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs. Methods In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B. Results Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm 2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm 2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm 2 ; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm 2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm 2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm 2 ; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873). Conclusions RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

items.title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year. METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT). RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days). CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

items.title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival. RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.
