items.title: Prevalence and intensity of chronic postsurgical pain after cranial surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized and non-randomized studies
items.abstract: Background/Importance Estimates of chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) after cranial surgery vary widely, and the prevalence and severity remain uncertain. Objectives To synthesize the literature and estimate the prevalence and intensity of CPSP after cranial surgery. Evidence reviews We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Web of Science up to April 2026 for randomized and non-randomized studies reporting CPSP (pain lasting ≥3 months) after cranial surgery. We performed random-effects meta-analysis and assessed the certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Findings 76 studies (13 740 patients) were included. Most studies evaluated tumor resection (54 of 76; 71%), and most patients underwent craniotomy (10 813 of 13 740; 79%). The median follow-up was 28.8 months (range 3 months to 16 years). Moderate-certainty evidence from 67 studies (10 607 patients) showed the pooled prevalence of CPSP at any severity is probably 27.4% (95% CI 20.8% to 34.6%; 95% prediction interval (PI) 0% to 85.8%). Moderate-certainty evidence from six studies that reported pain intensity (233 patients) showed the average pain intensity among patients who developed CPSP is probably 5.8 (95% CI 4.6 to 7.0; 95% PI 1.79 to 9.76) on a 0–10 Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Moderate-certainty evidence from 24 studies (4328 patients) showed the prevalence of moderate-to-severe CPSP (≥4/10 on a 0–10 NRS) is probably 16.7% (95% CI 12.8% to 20.9%; 95% PI 2.3% to 39.4%). Low-certainty evidence from 13 studies (3281 patients) suggests the prevalence of severe CPSP (≥7/10 on a 0–10 NRS) may be 5.9% (95% CI 3.0% to 9.8%; 95% PI 0% to 25.5%). Conclusions Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that CPSP probably affects approximately one in four patients after cranial surgery. Approximately one in six patients probably experience at least moderate pain (moderate certainty), and 1 in 17 may experience severe pain (low certainty). These findings underscore CPSP as a common complication after cranial surgery and highlight the need for prevention and management strategies. PROSPERO registration number CRD42024505270.

items.title: C2 suboccipital plane block (SOB-C2) for cervicogenic headache: a cadaveric study
items.abstract: Background and aims Cervicogenic headache is mediated by nociceptive input from upper cervical structures, including the C1–C3 spinal nerves, cervical joints, suboccipital muscles, and associated myodural bridges. The C2 dorsal root ganglion (DRG) represents an important convergence site within this nociceptive network. The suboccipital plane block targeting the C2 DRG (SOB-C2) has been described as an approach to these structures. This cadaveric study investigated the spread of injectate following SOB-C2 and determined whether the technique encompasses the suboccipital triangle and its neurovascular contents. Methods Bilateral ultrasound-guided SOB-C2 injections were performed in two unembalmed adult cadavers, yielding four hemispecimens. With the cadavers in the prone position, a needle was advanced in-plane from lateral to medial to a position deep to the obliquus capitis inferior muscle. A 2 mL of saline containing India ink was injected into each specimen. 1 hour after injection, layered anatomical dissection was performed to assess the distribution of injectate relative to the C2 DRG, suboccipital triangle, vertebral artery and C1–C2 joint. Results A tissue plane deep to the obliquus capitis inferior muscle was consistently identified in all four hemispecimens. Injectate staining consistently involved the deep surface of the obliquus capitis inferior muscle and its associated myodural bridges, the C2 DRG, and the floor of the suboccipital triangle, including the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane and underlying dura. The contents of the suboccipital triangle, particularly the vertebral artery were consistently stained. The posterior capsule of the C1–C2 joint was also stained in all specimens. The suboccipital nerve could not be reliably distinguished because of extensive staining within the triangle. Conclusions In this cadaveric study, the SOB-C2 injection consistently spread beyond the C2 DRG and myodural bridges to encompass the suboccipital triangle, including the vertebral artery with its surrounding sympathetic plexus, as well as the posterior capsule of the C1–C2 joint. These findings suggest that SOB-C2 may influence multiple anatomical structures implicated in cervicogenic headache. Further clinical and imaging studies are warranted to determine the clinical significance of this spread and to characterize the safety profile of the technique.

items.title: Assessment of preoperative gastric content with ultrasound in patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonists: an observational, multicenter, cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) delay gastric emptying, and there have been incidents of pulmonary aspiration in patients who had followed standard preoperative fasting instructions while on GLP-1 RA therapy. As the use of GLP-1 RAs is rising, we aim to compare the preoperative gastric contents of elective surgical patients taking GLP-1 RAs with those not taking these medications. Secondary objectives were to study the association of the indication, dose, time since last dose, and hours of fasting with gastric content. Methods This cross-sectional, multi-center study included elective surgery patients taking weekly GLP-1 RA medications for all indications, and those not taking them. All patients underwent standardized bedside gastric ultrasound preoperatively. Statistical analysis included χ2 or Fisher’s exact testing, Mann-Whitney U testing, and a multivariable logistic regression of full stomach on GLP-1 RA users, controlling for potential confounders where data were available. Results A total of 354 patients were enrolled from August 29, 2023, to January 31, 2025. A total of 307 patients were analyzed, 151 in the GLP-1 RA group, and 156 in the non-GLP-1 RA group. The occurrence of a full stomach was not significantly different between groups (13.9% vs 10.3%, p=0.38). Adjusted regression analysis also did not show a significant difference in fullness between groups (p=0.61). Patients in the GLP-1 RA group had a significantly longer solid fasting time than the non-GLP-1 RA group (median (Q1, Q3): 18.5 (13.5, 25.45) vs 15.98 (14.27, 17.55) hours; p=0.002). Treatment indication, time since last dose, and duration were not significantly associated with the occurrence of full stomach. Conclusions This study found no difference in the occurrence of full stomach in elective surgical patients taking GLP-1 RAs compared with the non-GLP-1 RA group. A longer solid fasting time in the GLP-1 RA group may have contributed to this finding. Our results also indicate that longer fasting times alone may not eliminate the risk of full stomach in patients taking GLP-1 RAs. Trial registration number NCT06003985.

items.title: Fluid dynamics of local anesthetic spread: a hypothesis-generating review
items.abstract: Background Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) have gained popularity for perioperative analgesia due to their simplicity and low complication rates, yet the anatomical and fluid-dynamic determinants of their injectate spread remain incompletely understood. A possible reason, so far largely unexamined, is that the biomechanics of fascial tissue and the fluid dynamics of injected solutions are poorly understood. Objective To introduce a theoretical, hypothesis-generating biophysical framework describing how fascial geometry, the viscoelastic properties of hyaluronan (HA)-rich fascial extracellular matrix, and injection parameters might influence spread of local anesthetics (LAs). None of the mechanisms discussed has been studied in patients receiving FPB, and the framework is offered as a research agenda rather than guidance for practice. Evidence review PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception to May 2026 for work on fascial geometry, HA, LA spread, and fluid mechanics of narrow and porous media. Because the mechanisms of interest have not been investigated in regional anesthesia, evidence was also drawn from biomechanics, tissue engineering, porous-media flow, Hele-Shaw cell research, and ophthalmic anesthesia (sub-Tenon block). Sources were selected for conceptual relevance with no formal assessment of study quality or risk of bias. Findings Two conventional modes of fluid propagation are distinguished: pressure-driven bulk-flow hydrodissection, initiating the initial anatomical distribution, and concentration-driven diffusion, acting later over a shorter distance. Hydrodynamic interfascial pattern-forming instabilities—of which viscous fingering is the best characterized—are proposed as a hypothesis, not as a third transport mechanism but as a pattern the advancing front may adopt during pressure-driven flow. In laboratory Hele-Shaw systems, a branched, fingering front fills a compartment with less work than a blunt front, but whether this occurs in living fascia is unknown. HA behaves as a non-Newtonian viscoelastic matrix whose rheology could modulate spread. Its postmortem degradation may contribute to the discrepancy between cadaveric and in vivo injectate patterns. Conclusions Recognizing HA as a dynamic functional matrix rather than merely a passive conduit for LA provides a theoretical explanation for the variability of FPBs. A strategy incorporating slow injection, warmed LA solution, real-time pressure monitoring, and the adjunctive use of hyaluronidase may promote more homogeneous distribution in experimental settings, but requires clinical validation.

items.title: Social determinants of health and outcomes after spinal cord stimulation: a retrospective cohort study
Quadratus lumborum block with or without subfascial wound catheter and post-caesarean delivery pain outcomes: a single-center retrospective cohort study (2026)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: We evaluated whether adding a subfascial wound catheter to a posterior quadratus lumborum block-based multimodal analgesic pathway improves pain and recovery after caesarean delivery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 361 women undergoing scheduled or urgent caesarean delivery from January to June 2026. All received bilateral posterior quadratus lumborum block and non-opioid multimodal analgesia; wound catheter use was optional. Ropivacaine infusion was continued for 48 h. Pain scores were recorded at 6, 24, and 48 h. Mobilisation, rescue analgesia, satisfaction, breastfeeding-related concern, breastfeeding outcomes, and repeat quadratus lumborum block were assessed. Catheter effects on pain were analysed using generalized estimating equations adjusted for anaesthetic technique, operative duration, repeat caesarean delivery, adhesions, age, and blood loss. RESULTS: Catheter use was associated with lower pain scores at 6 h (adjusted difference - 0.209, 95% confidence interval - 0.369 to -0.049; P = 0.011) and 24 h (-0.174, -0.309 to -0.039; P = 0.012), but not at 48 h (-0.016, -0.139 to 0.108; P = 0.805). These differences were too small to be clinically meaningful. Mobilisation, rescue analgesia, satisfaction, and breastfeeding outcomes were similar between groups. Breastfeeding-related concern was greater with catheter use. Repeat quadratus lumborum block was infrequently required and did not delay return to normal activity. DISCUSSION: Subfascial wound catheter use was not associated with clinically meaningful additional pain or recovery benefit. Patient counselling may help address breastfeeding-related concerns.

Understanding and improving the birth experience: the value of prospective structured perinatal audit and the Robson ten group classification system
The Evolution of Anesthesia for Congenital Heart Disease
items.abstract: This educational review describes the historical development of pediatric congenital cardiac anesthesia and its expanding role in the care of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Over the past eight decades, the specialty has evolved from an era in which few congenital heart defects were surgically treatable and perioperative mortality was high to one in which survival into adulthood is expected for most children with CHD. This transformation has been driven by parallel advances in surgical techniques, cardiopulmonary bypass technology, myocardial protection, monitoring, intensive care, and anesthetic management. From the first successful patent ductus arteriosus ligation in 1938 to the development of fetal cardiac interventions and the many major technological and scientific advances of the late twentieth and early twenty‐first centuries, anesthesiologists have played a pivotal role in improving the care of patients with CHD. As survival has improved, the population of adults and elderly patients living with repaired or palliated CHD has grown, and the specialty's focus has expanded beyond reducing perioperative mortality to improving lifelong outcomes. Today, congenital cardiac anesthesiologists are integral members of multidisciplinary teams responsible for perioperative risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, neuroprotection, coagulation management, mechanical circulatory support, and enhanced recovery. The history of the specialty highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continued scientific progress in improving patient safety, recovery, and long‐term outcomes.

items.title: Resilience Through Connection: A Group Coaching Framework for Women Anesthesiologists in the Women's Empowerment and Leadership Initiative ( WELI )
items.abstract: Background Women anesthesiologists face unique challenges that threaten their well‐being and retention. This includes high rates of imposter phenomenon, higher rates of attrition compared to male colleagues, and high rates of suicide. While group coaching is increasingly recognized as a developmental modality to foster growth in complex work environments, gaps remain in understanding how group coaching supports women who face imposter syndrome or how effective this modality is for women anesthesiologists. Aims This study examines the impact of a pilot group coaching intervention that focused on addressing imposter syndrome in women anesthesiologists participating in the Women's Empowerment and Leadership Initiative (WELI). Methods Fifteen women pediatric anesthesiologists, split across two groups, took part in seven monthly group coaching sessions. A post‐coaching survey was then conducted in which participants were asked about their experiences before and after group coaching. Eight of the participants volunteered to participate in semi‐structured interviews about their experiences. Qualitative data were coded using an inductive thematic analysis approach. Results The survey showed that following group coaching, participants demonstrated an increase in self‐reported compassion and acceptance of others. They also reported learning more about themselves and how to amend their own behavior in helpful ways compared to pre‐intervention. Two overarching themes emerged: a sense of community (fueled by psychological safety, validation, shared experience, and addressing imposter syndrome through the group coaching) and tools gained (including clearer priorities, work/life integration, and proactive social support). Conclusions Results of this pilot intervention suggest group coaching programs for anesthesiologists have the potential to build resilience in the current work environment, thereby benefiting not only individuals but the anesthesiology workforce as a whole.

items.title: Correlation of Neuron‐Specific Enolase and S100ß Protein Levels, Inflammatory Cytokines, and Neurological Injury in Children Undergoing Cardiopulmonary Bypass
items.abstract: Background The systemic inflammatory response syndrome to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) affects all organ systems including the brain. Perioperative brain injury in children with congenital heart disease is often clinically silent in the acute perioperative period and may not be detected until patients are older. The plasma biomarkers neuron‐specific enolase (NSE) and S100ß protein show potential for detecting neurological injury in the perioperative period. Objectives The three objectives of this study were to examine the correlation of NSE and S100ß protein levels with inflammatory cytokines, parameters of CPB, and the development of neurological injury in the intensive care unit following cardiac surgery in children. Methods 50 children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB had blood samples drawn at three time points: after induction of anesthesia, 30 min post‐CPB, and 24 h post‐CPB. Blood samples were analyzed for NSE, S100ß, and the inflammatory cytokines IL‐6, IL‐8, and IL‐10. Data were collected on CPB durations and neurological injury diagnosed in the postoperative period. Results NSE and S100ß increased significantly following bypass and correlated with increases of IL‐6, IL‐8, and IL‐10. There was a significant positive correlation of NSE and S100ß with duration of CPB, and of S100ß with duration of aortic cross clamp. Three patients suffered neurological insult. These patients had greater levels of NSE during the post‐CPB period ( p = 0.02) and S100ß at 24 h post‐CPB ( p = 0.02) than patients without neurological deficits. Conclusion The positive correlation between NSE, S100ß, inflammatory cytokines, and neurological deficits suggests that the systemic inflammatory response to CPB may contribute to neurological injury and that NSE and S100ß may be useful tools to detect neurological injury following CPB.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Risk Assessment Outcomes Are Associated With 30‐Day in Hospital Complications Following Pediatric Scoliosis Surgery: Evaluation of a Three‐Tiered Traffic‐Light Triage System at Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital
items.abstract: Background Scoliosis surgery is complex and associated with significant morbidity. Accurate risk assessment is essential for appropriate resource allocation and improved care. Risk factors for developing complications have been identified; however, structured frameworks to support preoperative assessment are limited. Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) uses a three‐tier multidisciplinary team (MDT) traffic‐light system to triage patients based on well‐defined risk factors and expert clinical judgment. Aim We aimed to describe complications following scoliosis surgery at GOSH and evaluate the relationship between preoperative MDT traffic‐light assessment and outcomes such as complication rates, operative times, and length of stay. Method A retrospective hospital file review was conducted for all patients presenting to GOSH for primary scoliosis surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Institutional approval was obtained, and the need for ethical approval was waived. Preoperative risk is quantified by the MDT using a three‐tier traffic‐light system categorizing patients as low (green), intermediate (amber), and high‐risk (red). Outcomes including 30‐day in‐hospital complications, operative time, and length of stay were analyzed in relation to preoperative MDT traffic‐light score. Results Of 350 eligible patients, 337 had a documented preoperative MDT traffic‐light assessment. Low‐risk patients comprised 43.6% ( n = 147/337), intermediate‐risk 49.3% ( n = 166/337), and high‐risk 7.1% ( n = 24/337). Major complications occurred in 2% ( n = 3/147) of low‐risk patients compared with 50% ( n = 12/24) of high‐risk patients, corresponding to an adjusted odds ratio of 11.4 ([95% CI 1.98–65.4], p = 0.006). High‐risk patients also had significantly longer operative times (381 min vs. 320 min, p < 0.001) and length of stay (12 days vs. 5 days, p < 0.001) when compared to low‐risk patients. Conclusion Patients classified as high‐risk by the MDT demonstrated an increased odds of developing major complications, longer operative time, and extended length of stay when compared to low‐risk patients. Similar structured tools, with local adaptations, may be valuable in other centers to support preoperative assessment, shared decision making, and guide resource allocation.

items.title: Regional Anesthesia for Pediatric Penile Surgery in Contemporary Practice: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study
Fidget and Sensory Toys for Anxiety and Emotional Regulation in Children: A Scoping Review With Implications for Pediatric Perioperative Care
items.abstract: Background Non‐pharmacological interventions are essential to reduce procedural anxiety in pediatric care. Fidget and sensory toys are widely used for distraction and self‐regulation, yet evidence on their effectiveness remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the evidence on fidget and sensory toys across general pediatric settings, with a focus on perioperative outcomes—such as anxiety, distress, and pain—to highlight relevant gaps in care. Methods This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA‐ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL, complemented by trial registries, gray literature, citation tracking, and reference screening. Studies involving children (0–18 years) evaluating fidget or sensory toys in any setting were eligible. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Findings Fifteen studies published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Fidget spinners were the most frequently investigated device ( n = 9), followed by stress balls ( n = 3). Studies were conducted in educational ( n = 8) and healthcare settings ( n = 7). Educational studies generally reported limited or no benefits for attention, engagement, behavior, or academic performance. In contrast, healthcare studies generally suggested reductions in anxiety, pain, fear, and procedural distress, although findings were heterogeneous, and outcome measures varied substantially. Conclusions Current evidence does not support the routine use of fidget toys to improve attention or academic performance in educational settings. Evidence from healthcare and procedural settings suggests that fidget and sensory toys may be feasible distraction tools for selected pediatric patients, but evidence is insufficient to support routine perioperative use. Further high‐quality randomized controlled trials are needed to establish standardized intervention protocols and identify the pediatric populations and clinical settings most likely to benefit.

items.title: Neonatal Spinal Anesthetic LAST : Case Unproven
Preoperative Oral Esketamine for Perioperative Comfort in Children Undergoing Adenotonsillectomy: A Randomized, Double‐Blind, Dose‐Finding Study
items.abstract: Background Pediatric adenotonsillectomy often causes preoperative anxiety, venous cannulation pain, and emergence agitation. Esketamine has multimodal properties, but the optimal oral dose for children is unknown. This study evaluated oral esketamine at 1, 2, and 3 mg/kg for perioperative comfort. Methods In this randomized double‐blind trial, 99 children (ASA I–II, 1–6 years) received oral 10% glucose (control, n = 26) or esketamine 1 mg/kg (EK1, n = 26), 2 mg/kg (EK2, n = 23), or 3 mg/kg (EK3, n = 24) 30 min before anesthesia. Primary outcomes: Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) and FLACC pain score at venous cannulation, and PAED score at 15 min after extubation. Secondary outcomes: remifentanil use, postoperative FLACC (2–48 h), sleep quality, and adverse events. Results All esketamine doses improved sedation and analgesia at cannulation (overall p < 0.001), with largest effect at 3 mg/kg. Median RSS (IQR): control 1.00 (1.00–2.00); EK1 2.00 (1.75–3.00, p = 0.028); EK2 2.00 (1.00–3.00, p = 0.049); EK3 3.00 (2.00–3.37, p < 0.001). FLACC scores: control 6.00 (3.00–7.00); EK1 2.50 (1.00–4.00, p = 0.016); EK2 2.00 (0.00–4.00, p = 0.001); EK3 0.00 (0.00–1.75, p < 0.001). PAED score at 15 min was lower in EK2 than control (5.00 [2.00–10.00] vs. 10.00 [6.00–12.00], p = 0.048). Remifentanil consumption was reduced in EK3 (120.00 [80.00–159.50] vs. 240.00 [160.00–315.00] μg, p = 0.001). Postoperative pain at 2–6 h was lower in EK2 and EK3 ( p < 0.05), persisting to 48 h in EK3 ( p < 0.05). Sleep quality improved in EK3 at 24 h ( p = 0.023) and 48 h ( p = 0.032). Adverse events did not differ significantly. Conclusions Preoperative oral esketamine (1–3 mg/kg) enhances perioperative comfort in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy. The 2 mg/kg dose offers the best balance of efficacy and safety, while 3 mg/kg provides superior analgesia and opioid sparing.

items.title: Ultrasound‐Guided Supraclavicular Brachiocephalic Vein Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Hematological Disorders: A Retrospective Comparative Study
items.abstract: Background Central venous access is indispensable for clinical management of pediatric patients with hematological disorders, including chemotherapy administration, blood product transfusion, and critical rescue. Repeated venipuncture attempts, procedural failure, postoperative catheter malposition, and cannulation‐related complications can substantially disrupt subsequent treatment courses and compromise therapeutic efficacy. Aims This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of ultrasound‐guided brachiocephalic vein (BCV) cannulation, with the goal of optimizing central venous catheterization protocols, reducing procedure‐related adverse events, and improving the efficiency and safety of treatment via central venous access in pediatric patients. Methods This retrospective study included 580 children (303 subclavian vein [SCV], 277 BCV) who underwent ultrasound‐guided central venous catheterization between January 2021 and December 2024. We compared first‐attempt success rate, overall success rate, procedural duration, intraoperative adverse events, postoperative complications, and catheter malposition. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to improve comparability between the groups with respect to measured baseline covariates. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Results After IPTW, the BCV approach was associated with a higher first‐attempt success rate (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.05–2.81; risk difference [RD] = 0.119, 95% CI: 0.015–0.222) and a higher overall success rate (RD = 0.091, 95% CI: 0.013–0.168). The mean procedural duration was 6 min shorter in the BCV group (95% CI: −9.5 to −2.5). The BCV approach was independently associated with lower odds of intraoperative malposition (OR = 0.096, 95% CI: 0.037–0.249), postoperative malposition (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.16–0.74), and perioperative complications (OR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.08–0.94). Multivariable regression analysis showed that catheterization approach was independently associated with catheter malposition. Conclusions Compared with SCV, ultrasound‐guided BCV cannulation is associated with higher success rates, shorter procedural duration, and fewer malpositions and complications. This technique may offer particular benefits for children with hematological disorders.

items.title: Intravenous Lidocaine in Children: French Practice, Barriers to Use, and the Need for Pharmacokinetic Data
Comparing Subglottic Ultrasound and Distal Phalanx Width for Pediatric Endotracheal Tube Sizing in a Predominantly School‐Aged Pediatric Cohort: A Prospective Study
items.abstract: Background Accurate endotracheal tube (ETT) sizing is essential in pediatric airway management to optimize ventilation and reduce complications. Traditional methods, including age‐based formulas and distal phalanx width (DPW), may lack precision. Subglottic ultrasound (US) has emerged as a promising tool, but its predictive accuracy compared with DPW remains unclear. This study aimed to compare accuracy, agreement, diagnostic performance, and clinical applicability of subglottic US versus DPW for predicting optimal ETT size in children, while recognizing that the enrolled cohort was predominantly school‐aged. Methods In this prospective observational study, pediatric patients aged 0–12 years undergoing elective or emergency intubation were assessed. Pre‐intubation measurements included subglottic transverse airway diameter by ultrasound (ACUSON Juniper, microconvex probe, 5–10 MHz) and DPW by digital calipers. Predicted ETT sizes were compared with the final clinically accepted cuffed ETT inner diameter confirmed by leak testing and cuff pressure optimization. Agreement was evaluated using Bland–Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, while diagnostic performance was defined a priori as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Logistic regression identified predictors of good ETT fit. Results Among 160 patients, the median age was 8.8 years (IQR 7.0–10.5), indicating predominance of older children. Ultrasound‐predicted ETT size showed a stronger correlation with actual size ( r = 0.479, p < 0.001) than DPW ( r = 0.248, p = 0.002). Ultrasound predictions had narrower Bland–Altman limits of agreement, although ultrasound measurement is operator‐dependent. DPW showed poor sensitivity (5.9%) but high specificity (99.3%) for identifying underfit ETTs, with limited overall discrimination (ROC AUC = 0.53). Only subglottic diameter was a significant predictor of good ETT fit. Conclusion Subglottic ultrasound showed better agreement with clinically accepted ETT size than DPW in this predominantly school‐aged pediatric cohort. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound as an adjunct to pediatric airway assessment, but conclusions should be interpreted cautiously in infants and younger children because they were under‐represented. Standardized measurement protocols and operator training are needed before broad implementation.

items.title: Milestones in Motion: Ectopic Pregnancy
Progesterone Receptor Antagonists for Labor Induction
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate mifepristone, a progesterone receptor antagonist, for labor induction and cesarean delivery and related measures of maternal and neonatal safety. DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses) 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251236886). MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Scopus were searched through October 2025. METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included randomized trials evaluating mifepristone for labor induction in singleton pregnancies at 37 weeks or more of gestation. Studies involving pregnancy termination, intrauterine fetal death, preterm induction, or concomitant cervical ripening interventions in which the effects of mifepristone could not be isolated were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included induction-to-delivery interval, time to labor onset, Bishop score, need for prostaglandin or oxytocin, postpartum hemorrhage, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and 5-minute Apgar score less than 7. Data were pooled with a random-effects model. TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: The primary analysis included all 15 eligible randomized controlled trials across mifepristone dosing regimens (n=1,063) and control conditions (n=811). Mifepristone was associated with 33% reduced odds of cesarean delivery (33.1% vs 41.9%, odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI, 0.54–0.82) compared with the control method of induction. Mifepristone was associated with higher Bishop scores at 24 hours, shorter induction-to-delivery intervals, and less prostaglandin and oxytocin use compared with control methods. Findings were similar in sensitivity analysis limited to placebo-controlled and high-quality trials (cesarean delivery odds ratio 0.58, 95% CI, 0.40–0.83). No differences were observed in postpartum hemorrhage, NICU admission, or low Apgar score, although most studies did not report these outcomes. CONCLUSION: Use of mifepristone for labor induction was associated with reduced odds of cesarean delivery, as well as improved cervical ripening and labor induction efficiency. No evidence of short-term maternal or neonatal risk was found, although robust data were limited. Findings support the role of progesterone antagonists for labor induction. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO, CRD420251236886.

items.title: Risk Factors and Associated Severe Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality at Cesarean Delivery for the Second Twin
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between cesarean delivery for the second twin after vaginal delivery of the first twin and severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in comparison with vaginal delivery, and, secondarily, to identify risk factors for second twin cesarean delivery. METHODS: This was a planned secondary analysis of the JUMODA (JUmeaux MODe d'Accouchement) cohort, a national prospective population-based study of twin deliveries conducted from February 2014 to March 2015 in 176 French maternities. For this analysis, we included only second twins born after vaginal delivery of the first twin at a gestational of at least 32 weeks. The primary outcome was severe neonatal morbidity and mortality. The association of cesarean delivery for the second twin with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in the total population was estimated from multivariate Poisson regression models. A sensitivity analysis limited to pregnancies that mirrored the Twin Birth Study low-risk population was conducted. Candidate risk factors were evaluated for cesarean delivery for the second twin. RESULTS: Among the 3,905 second twins included in analysis, 124 (3.2%) were delivered by cesarean and 3,781 (96.8%) were delivered vaginally. Cesarean delivery for the second twin was associated with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality compared with vaginal delivery (n=11/24 [8.9%] vs n=95/3,781 [2.5%]; adjusted relative risk [aRR] 3.17, 95% CI, 1.58–6.40). Findings were similar in the low-risk population (n=8/106 [7.5%] vs n=62/3,230 [1.9%]; aRR 4.03, 95% CI, 1.97–8.24). Absence of locoregional analgesia (aRR 2.13, 95% CI, 1.18–2.86), transverse second twin presentation (aRR 2.11, 95% CI, 1.44–3.08), and delivery in centers that performed fewer than 50 twin deliveries per year (aRR 1.58, 95% CI, 1.01–2.48) were associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery for the second twin. Conversely, breech second twin presentation was a protective factor (aRR 0.47, 95% CI, 0.27–0.82). CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of twin deliveries that involved vaginal delivery of the first twin, cesarean delivery for the second twin tripled the risk of severe neonatal morbidity and mortality when compared with vaginal delivery. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the small number of events and potential residual confounding.

items.title: Modeling the U.S. National Burden of Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the national burden of severe hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) attributed to the three most clinically significant alloantibodies (anti-D, anti-K, and anti-c) using a large data set of prenatal antibody screens in U.S. pregnancies. METHODS: Prenatal red blood cell alloantibody results were extracted from a national laboratory firm from 2010 to 2021 and normalized to the U.S. population race, ethnicity, and regional distributions based on Census data. Prevalence of critical alloantibody titers, pregnancy continuation rates, distribution of paternal race and ethnicity, allele prevalence of antigen in paternal race and ethnicity, and rate of disease were used to estimate the burden of disease using Monte Carlo simulations. RESULTS: There were 8,809,993 pregnancies included in the cohort. Normalization of the cohort to U.S. births resulted in an estimated national prevalence of any high-risk antibodies of 686.5 per 100,000 pregnancies (27.9 per 100,000 for anti-c, 596.1 per 100,000 for anti-D, and 62.5 per 100,000 for anti-K), with 63.9 per 100,000 (1.9 for anti-c, 20.6 for anti-D, and 41.3 for anti-K) of those reaching critical levels. The estimated national burden of severe HDFN attributed to any high-risk antibody was 2.4 per 100,000 pregnancies (95% CI, 2.0–2.9). Among all pregnancies with critical titers, 3.8% (95% CI, 3.1–4.5) were estimated to result in severe HDFN. CONCLUSION: This study provides contemporary national estimates of severe HDFN in the United States, demonstrating that, although alloimmunization is relatively common, progression to severe HDFN remains rare.

items.title: Anti-Müllerian Hormone Trajectories Across the Menopause Transition
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the trajectory of anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) decline leading to the final menstrual period, identify distinct AMH patterns, and assess their association with unique participant characteristics. METHODS: SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation), a multisite, multiethnic perimenopausal cohort, was analyzed. Included participants had an observed final menstrual period and three or more measurements of AMH levels taken during perimenopause. Statistical modeling was used to identify AMH trajectory classes; participants were placed into predicted class based on best fit. Differences in baseline demographic and health characteristics were assessed by analysis of variance or χ 2 . Generalized estimating equation models were used to estimate the association between AMH trajectory class and outcomes, accounting for repeated measures. RESULTS: A total of 1,131 women had at least three AMH measurements and an observed final menstrual period. Two AMH trajectory classes were observed: 448 participants (39.6%) with lower initial AMH and slower decline (low/slow [LS] group) and 683 participants (60.4%) with higher AMH and steeper decline (high/fast [HF] group). Participants in the LS group had a median AMH decline of 1.2 pg/mL/month; those in the HF group had a decline of 6.7 pg/mL/month. The LS classification was associated with baseline older age, higher body mass index (BMI), and non-White race and ethnicity. Trajectory classes did not differ by history of oligomenorrhea, presumptive polycystic ovarian syndrome, or smoking status. Participants in the LS group had worse postmenopausal cardiovascular risk profiles and were less likely to report frequent vasomotor symptoms after the final menstrual period. CONCLUSION: Two different AMH trajectories to the final menstrual period were observed in a subsample of SWAN participants. Independent of a participant's premenopausal cardiovascular risk factors, lower starting AMH and slower decline were associated with higher postmenopausal cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Antidepressant Discontinuation During Pregnancy and Risk of Mental Health–Related Emergencies
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate contemporary patterns of antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy and associated maternal mental health outcomes, including behavioral health–related emergency department (ED) visits, among patients with preexisting depression or anxiety. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of a state-based private insurance claims database in Pennsylvania. Patients who delivered between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, with a diagnosis of depression or anxiety before pregnancy and an active prescription for a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) in the 3 months before pregnancy were included. The exposure was antidepressant continuation compared with discontinuation during pregnancy, defined as no prescription fills or a gap of more than 60 days. The primary outcome was behavioral health–related ED visits during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Behavioral health–related ED visit rates were compared between patients who continued and those who discontinued antidepressants with appropriate bivariate statistical tests. RESULTS: Among 3,983 patients with depression or anxiety, 1,462 (36.7%) entered pregnancy with an active SSRI or SNRI prescription. Of these, 260 (17.8%) had no medication fills during pregnancy, and 945 (64.6%) had a gap of more than 60 days. Among patients with a treatment gap of more than 60 days, discontinuation occurred most commonly in the first trimester (44.9%) followed by the third trimester (30.3%). Patients who continued and those who discontinued treatment had similar rates of outpatient and ED mental health visits before pregnancy. However, discontinuation was associated with a higher risk of mental health–related emergency visits during pregnancy, with peaks in the second month (58 vs 37/1,000, P =.027) and the ninth month (59 vs 29/1,000, P <.01) of pregnancy. This increased risk persisted postpartum, with higher rates of mental health–related ED visits within 8 months after delivery among those who discontinued treatment during pregnancy (32 vs 21/1,000, P =.02). CONCLUSION: In this cohort of privately insured patients with preexisting depression or anxiety, antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy was common and was associated with increased risk of mental health–related ED visits. These findings underscore the need for clinical and policy strategies to support continuation of evidence-based treatment for perinatal mental health conditions and to address preventable contributors to maternal morbidity and mortality.

items.title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system–wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum. METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021–May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024–August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed. RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% ( P =.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% ( P <.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P =.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally. CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

items.title: Prenatal Maternal Phosphatidylcholine and Children’s Behavior and Cognition through 4 Years of Age: Randomized Clinical Trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. Rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7 , associated with Schizophrenia, Attention Deficit Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7 , convey risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age. Objective To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and increase cognitive performance. Study Design A clinical trial at University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by parents on the Child Behavior Check List 1.5-5-year version (CBCL 1.5-5yr ). The 2 primary outcomes were Withdrawn and Attention Problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-IV Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (Full Scale-IQ). Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed phosphatidylcholine's fetal developmental effects. Results Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared to placebo produced fewer children with multiple or pervasive Withdrawn problems and increased WPPSI-IV Full-Scale IQ (mean difference 7.78, 95% CI 1.88, 13.7; p=.010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly. In exploratory analyses, 11 children had CBCL 1.5-5yr Autism Spectrum T-scores in the clinical referral range and language deficits typical of Autism Spectrum Disorder, 10 of 71 from women who had placebo and 1 of 71 who had phosphatidylcholine, Risk Ratio 10.0; 95% CI 1.31, 76.1; p=.026. Twelve children had Full-Scale IQ > 120 (>90 %ile), 10 of 54 from women who had phosphatidylcholine and 2 of 49 who had placebo, Risk Ratio 4.54; 95% CI 1.05, 19.7; p=.044. Positive effects were observed regardless of presence or absence of maternal mental disorders. Phosphatidylcholine produced no significant adverse effects or safety problems for women or children. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypertension were not increased. The children had normal physical parameters at birth and through childhood. Several limitations temper the study's findings: effects on Attention problems did not reach significance, parents rated social behavior, and one-third of women were lost between prenatal enrollment and 4-year assessments. Conclusion Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements provide safe, effective support of fetal brain development. Comparison of doses from this and previous trials suggests 6300 mg phosphatidylcholine or 900 mg choline, beginning as early as possible in gestation. Outcomes for the children include fewer social withdrawal problems and increased cognitive test performance.

items.title: Bladder Neck Versus Midurethral Placement of Retropubic Autologous Fascial Slings: A Systematic Review
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare objective and subjective cure/improvement rates and surgical outcomes of female patients with stress or mixed urinary incontinence undergoing autologous retropubic pubovaginal slings between traditional bladder neck sling placement and midurethral sling placement. DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of Medline, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted using standardized MeSH terms from conception to March 2025 (PROSPERO-registered). Studies underwent double screening, and a third reviewer resolved any discrepancies. STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating outcomes of retropubic autologous slings for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) or mixed urinary incontinence (MUI). Studies published in English or French were eligible for inclusion. We included slings performed for recurrent SUI or MUI, as well as those placed concomitantly with prolapse surgery, providing a minimum postoperative follow-up of six weeks was reported. We excluded systematic reviews, meta-analyses, review articles, case reports, studies lacking details on surgical approach or sling material, and studies evaluating non-autologous slings. STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: We evaluated study quality using RoB, the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials, and the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (NIH) Quality Assessment Tool for Observational Cohort and Cross-Sectional Studies. We present odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals to estimate the effect of sling placement location on each outcome through random-effect logistic regression. RESULTS: We screened 5578 abstracts, assessed 233 full texts for eligibility, and retained 61 studies. 13 of these were randomized controlled trials and 48 were observational studies. Objective (74.0% vs. 81.1%, OR 1.10 [0.37-3.28]) and subjective cure (70.8% vs. 58.6 %, OR 0.46 [0.19-1.10]) were not statistically significantly different between bladder neck vs. midurethral placement of retropubic autologous fascial sling at a median of 2.4 years [0.3-6.8] postoperatively. Objective improvement (90.5% vs.84.5%, OR 0.41 [0.10-1.67]) and subjective improvement (85.9% vs. 85.1%, OR 0.77 [0.31-1.92]) rates were also similar between the groups. Most adverse events were similar between groups except midurethral placement was associated with a lower risk of de novo urgency (15.0% vs 8.3%, OR 0.50 [0.26-0.96]). Study quality assessment using the RoB tool for RCT and the NIH Quality Assessment of Observational Control and Cross-Sectional studies overall revealed a moderate to high risk of bias among included studies. CONCLUSION: Bladder neck and midurethral placements of autologous slings have similar surgical success and adverse effects rates, with the exception of de novo urgency which favours midurethral sling placement. A randomized controlled trial is required to confirm these findings.

items.title: IVF versus surgery for infertility in women with deep and ovarian endometriosis: a partially randomized patient preference trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Study objective Endometriosis-associated infertility can be managed either surgically or through assisted reproductive technologies (ART). Given the recent substantial improvement in the accuracy of ultrasound diagnosis of ovarian endometriomas and deep infiltrating endometriosis, surgery is no longer required to detect these disease forms. Therefore, infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed endometriosis face two alternatives; they can be either operated or straight embark in in vitro fertilization (IVF). In this study, we aimed to compare these two options, as no randomized clinical trial (RCT) has yet addressed this clinical scenario. Study design A multicenter, pragmatic, partially randomized patient preference trial (PRPT) was conducted at three Italian tertiary referral centers with expertise in both endometriosis surgery and IVF. The trial was designed to compare reproductive outcomes between IVF and surgery in infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian and deep infiltrating endometriosis. Women with a history of previous surgery for endometriosis or prior IVF were excluded. Additional key eligibility criteria were age Results Recruitment began in March 2021 and was discontinued in September 2024 in accordance with the Ethics Committees after the enrollment of 130 women (55 in the randomized cohort and 75 in the preference cohort), owing to investigators' increasing awareness of a markedly higher likelihood of success in women allocated to IVF. In the randomized cohort, the number of live births observed in the surgical and IVF groups was 7 out of 27 (26%) and 16 out of 28 (57%), respectively (p=0.019). The RR of live birth in women assigned to IVF was 2.20 (95% CI, 1.08-4.50). In the preference cohort, the number of live births was 7 out of 25 (28%) and 32 out of 50 (64%), respectively (p=0.003). The relative risks (RR) of live birth for women assigned to IVF in the randomized and preference cohorts were 2.20 (95% CI: 1.08-4.50) and 2.29 (95% CI: 1.18-4.43), respectively. When data from the two cohorts were combined, the RR remained consistent at 2.29 (95% CI: 1.41-3.70). Per protocol and survival analyses further supported these findings. Conclusions In this pragmatic PRPT, IVF was more effective than surgery for the treatment of infertility in women with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian or deep infiltrating endometriosis.

items.title: Assessing the Safety of Estro-Progestin and Progestin-only drugs: A Signal Detection Study of Meningioma Reports in EudraVigilance
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exogenous hormonal therapies are used for contraception and for several gynecologic and menopausal indications, frequently for prolonged periods. Previous epidemiological studies have reported an increased risk of meningioma with some progestins, particularly following prolonged exposure and high cumulative doses. It is a common intracranial tumor with marked female predominance, suggesting a potential role of hormones in its pathogenesis and growth. Most meningiomas are located in the anterior or middle skull base, where a higher prevalence of progesterone receptors has been observed. This evidence further underlines the relationship between hormonal factors and this type of intracranial tumor. Moreover, rapid and spontaneous tumor regression has been reported after cessation of treatment with exogenous hormones or when serum progestogen levels decrease due to physiological factors. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the presence of a safety signal for meningioma among users of estro-progestin and progestin-only therapies using pharmacovigilance data. STUDY DESIGN: Data from the EudraVigilance database were analyzed using both descriptive and statistical approaches. Three complementary disproportionality methods were applied to strengthen signal detection: Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR), Information Component (IC), and Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EBGM). The study period covered the last ten years, from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025. The drugs analyzed included: drospirenone-ethinylestradiol combination, dienogest-ethinylestradiol combination, drospirenone-only, desogestrel and levonorgestrel. We included all reports in which these drugs were recorded as suspected, excluding those in which they were reported only as concomitant drugs. RESULTS: A total of 21,091 reports, corresponding to 70,476 drug-ADR pairs, were identified. As expected, most reports concerned female patients, consistent with both the indication of these therapies and the known higher prevalence of meningioma in women. Disproportionality signals were identified for drospirenone and desogestrel-only formulations, suggesting a potential association with meningioma: A disproportionality signal was identified for desogestrel-only pills (110 reports; ROR 11.11, 95% CI 8.79-14.06; IC025 2.64; EB05 5.79). A novel exploratory signal also emerged for drospirenone-only pills (8 reports; ROR 2.41, 95% CI 1.19-4.89; IC025 0.54; EB05 1.17). No disproportionality signal was detected for the two combined formulations or levonorgestrel; absence of a signal should not be interpreted as absence of risk or evidence of comparative safety. In addition to meningioma, other serious adverse drug reactions - including known cardiovascular events and previously unreported reactions - were identified, warranting further investigation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of ongoing pharmacovigilance activities and careful benefit-risk evaluation of hormonal therapies, particularly given their widespread and long-term use and the potential for rare but serious outcomes such as meningioma. This analysis identified new but exploratory safety signals that warrant confirmation in studies with valid exposure denominators, longitudinal treatment histories, latency assessment, and control of confounding. The findings should not be used alone to infer causality or guide comparative clinical decisions.

items.title: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure with or without intraoperative iodine: A randomized controlled trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix (IOS) during loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) is commonly used to better define surgical resection margins. No randomized head-to-head comparison of LEEP with vs without IOS is available to inform clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To compare LEEP with versus without IOS regarding rates of involved resection margins, patient satisfaction and procedure-related outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: Consecutive women referred to a university colposcopy unit were recruited and randomized 1:1 to LEEP with intraoperative application of Lugol's iodine or LEEP without intraoperative Lugol's iodine (control). The primary endpoint was the histopathological rate of involved resection margins. Secondary endpoints included patient satisfaction assessed on the day of surgery and 14 days thereafter using numerical rating scales (0-10) and procedure-related complications, pain, blood loss, and surgeon preference. Results were compared using nonparametric, chi-square, and t tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the influence of covariates on the primary outcome. RESULTS: Between January 2022 and September 2025, we randomized 229 women, 114 in the IOS arm and 115 in the control arm. In an intention-to-treat analysis, rates of involved resection margins were 20/114 (17.5%) vs 8/115 (7.0%) (risk difference, 10.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.1-19.3; risk ratio, 2.52; 95% CI 1.16-5.49; P=.014). Post hoc analysis of 215 women showed lower main-cone depth after fixation with IOS (transformation-zone-adjusted mean difference, -1.47 mm; 95% CI, -2.61 to -0.34; P=.011). There were no differences in operative metrics including cone weight, cone fragmentation, procedure time, and time to complete hemostasis. Intraoperative complications were similar in both groups as were surgeons' ratings. Immediate postoperative pain and satisfaction did not differ significantly between groups. At 14-day follow-up, bleeding outcomes favored the iodine group. Bleeding intensity during the first 24 postoperative hours was lower (median 1 [interquartile range 0-3] vs 2 [1-4]; P=.008) and bleeding duration was shorter (median 3 [1-9] vs 5 [2-14] days; P=.047). There were no differences in pain intensity, pain duration, analgesic use, or overall satisfaction at follow-up. In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, body mass index, ever smoking, and transformation zone, randomization to IOS remained associated with higher odds of involved resection margins (adjusted odds ratio 3.46, 95% CI 1.38-8.70; P=.008). CONCLUSION: LEEP with IOS is associated with a higher rate of involved resection margins and should therefore not be used routinely in clinical practice.

items.title: Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence and survival of uterine sarcomas by histotype, race and ethnicity in the United States, 2000–2019
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Uterine sarcomas are rare but aggressive mesenchymal malignancies of the uterus, characterized by diverse histotypes and poor survival. However, little is known about the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of uterine sarcoma histotypes at the population level. Objective To evaluate hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates and five-year relative survival by histologic subtype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity among U.S. individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma in the SEER 22 registries from 2000-2019. Study design This retrospective population-based study included microscopically confirmed uterine sarcoma cases registered in the SEER 22 database. Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates were calculated by histotype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity. Five-year relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method in SEER*Stat software (version 9.0.42). Results A total of 14,801 individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma were included. Leiomyosarcoma (LMS) were most common comprising 53.3% of the total cases (n=7883), endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) accounted for 26.7% of cases (n=3948), Adenosarcoma for 12.7% (n=1884), sarcoma not otherwise specified (NOS) for 5.7% (n=837), and undifferentiated sarcoma for 1.7% of cases (n=249). Incidence rates of uterine sarcomas increased until ages 50-54 and plateaued thereafter other than among Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) individuals, where incidence continued to increase until ages 65-69 years. LMS demonstrated the highest hysterectomy-corrected incidence (0.6 per 100,000), followed by ESS (0.3 per 100,000) and Adenosarcoma (0.1 per 100,000). NHB individuals had the highest incidence of uterine sarcomas across all histotypes. Overall, NHB individuals were more likely to be diagnosed with distant diseases compared with other groups. Among all individuals, five-year relative survival was 42.3% (95% CI: 41-43.5) for LMS, 70.2% (68.5-71.8) for ESS, and 78.3% (75.7-80.6) for Adenosarcoma. When categorized by stage at diagnosis, relative survival for localized disease ranged from 62% to 85% in all histotypes, vs. 13.5% to 34.7% for distant metastatic disease. Survival was lowest among NHB individuals, 41.9%, versus 55.4 % in Non-Hispanic White (NHW) individuals, across all histotypes and stage at diagnosis. Conclusion Uterine sarcomas exhibit pronounced heterogeneity, comprising distinct histotypes that demonstrate variable incidence patterns and survival trajectories. LMS had the highest incidence and worse survival compared with ESS and Adenosarcoma. NHB individuals had the highest incidence rates for all histotypes and were more likely to have advanced disease and worse survival compared with other groups. Future studies are required to evaluate underlying risk factors, early detection strategies, and response to therapy by histotype, with a particular focus on addressing disparities in NHB individuals.

items.title: Evening Phone Use and Sleep Outcomes Among Youth
items.abstract: Importance Smartphone use has been associated with poor sleep, but existing evidence primarily relies on self-reported, cross-sectional data. Objective To examine within-person and between-person associations between passively sensed evening smartphone use and objectively measured sleep outcomes in adolescents. Design, Setting, and Participants This intensive longitudinal cohort study assessed passively sensed data from US youths in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study. Participants were Android users with at least 14 days of concurrent Effortless Assessment Research System application data and Fitbit-measured sleep. Data were collected between November 30, 2020, and February 5, 2024, and analyzed from February 2 to June 1, 2026. Analysis used within-between decomposition in multilevel models to separate within-person from between-person associations. Exposures Smartphone use after each hourly cutoff from 8 pm to midnight (cumulative) and within 5 to 30 minutes before sleep onset (proximal) were quantified. Main Outcomes and Measures Fitbit-derived sleep measures were assessed, including total sleep time (TST), onset, offset, and sustained and total wake after sleep onset (WASO). Results A total of 425 participants (mean [SD] age, 14.8 [1.1] years; 216 [50.8%] female) contributed 7591 person-nights of data. On nights when adolescents used their phones more than their own evening average (after 10 pm ), they slept a mean (SD) of 20.05 (49.42) minutes less and fell asleep a mean (SD) of approximately 64.73 (50.95) minutes later. Adjusting for covariates, within-person analyses revealed that each additional minute of smartphone use after 10 pm above a participant’s own average was associated with sleep onset that was 0.87 (95% CI, 0.84 to 0.90) minutes later, sleep offset that was 0.37 (95% CI, 0.33 to 0.41) minutes later, and a TST change of −0.43 (95% CI, −0.47 to −0.39) minutes (all P &lt; .001). Estimates increased monotonically across cutoffs from 8 pm to midnight. Proximal use was associated with greater sustained WASO, largest in the final 5 minutes of use before sleep onset (0.74 [95% CI, 0.50 to 0.98] additional minutes of wakefulness; P &lt; .001) and negligible when looking at the final 20 minutes of use before sleep onset. This association was concentrated in the first 30 minutes after sleep onset. Conclusions and Relevance This cohort study found that greater cumulative late-evening phone use was associated with later sleep onset, delayed sleep offset, and shorter TST. Smartphone use immediately before sleep onset was associated with greater WASO, primarily during the first 30 minutes after sleep onset. These findings suggest that reducing evening smartphone use, particularly after 10 pm and immediately before bedtime, may help improve sleep health in adolescents.

items.title: Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) for Youth With Prolonged Concussion Recovery
items.abstract: Importance Research suggests that aerobic exercise improves recovery for youth with concussion; however, prior studies primarily focused on acute concussion and required multiple in-person visits. Objective To determine whether a virtually delivered aerobic exercise program improves recovery following concussion compared to a stretching control and examine potential moderators. Design, Setting, and Participants A randomized clinical trial was conducted from 2021 to 2025 comparing the Mobile Subthreshold Exercise Program (MSTEP) to a stretching control for 11- to 18-year-olds with concussion up to 1 year from injury. Participants were recruited from a variety of outpatient locations in 4 US states (Washington, Utah, Wisconsin, and Oregon). Recruitment and data collection occurred from March 2021 until October 2025, and data analysis occurred from November 2025 to April 2026. Interventions Youth randomized to MSTEP were provided activity trackers and an aerobic exercise program initiated at 60% of heart rate maximum. Exercise was advanced in intensity and duration over 6 weeks through weekly videoconferencing calls. Youth in the control group were given stretching exercises and similar weekly calls. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes included (1) concussive symptoms and (2) health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Secondary outcomes included sleep, depression, and anxiety. Moderation by sex, age, and time since injury was examined. Patients were followed up for 6 months. Results The sample included 210 participants, among whom 122 (58.1%) were female, mean (SD) age was 15.1 (2.2) years, and mean (SD) time since injury was 73.3 (63.3) days. Covariate-adjusted regression analysis showed significant improvement in concussive symptoms and HRQoL at all time points, with greater improvement in MSTEP compared to control at the 3-month time point for both concussive symptoms (β, −3.15; 95% CI, −6.05 to −0.25; adjusted P = .04) and HRQoL (β, 4.15; 95% CI, 0.64-7.66; adjusted P = .04). No significant differences by group were seen at 6 months. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling with exponential decay showed significantly faster symptom recovery in MSTEP compared to control (difference in rates, −0.68; 95% CI, −2.22 to −0.04; P = .002). Secondary outcomes (sleep, depression, and anxiety) improved in all participants but were not different by group. Benefit of the intervention was only significant for individuals less than 3 months from injury (concussive symptoms: β, −4.44; 95% CI, −7.99 to −0.90; unadjusted P = .01; HRQoL: β, 6.64; 95% CI, 2.55-10.72; unadjusted P = .002). No evidence was found for moderation by other factors. Conclusions and Relevance Per the results of this randomized clinical trial, an aerobic exercise program improves speed of recovery following concussion for youth compared to stretching and can be delivered remotely. However, this type of program appears to be most beneficial for individuals with acute or subacute injury (&lt;3 months since injury). Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04688255

items.title: Ambulatory Electrocardiography Modalities in Pediatric Arrhythmia Detection and Management
items.abstract: Importance The diagnostic efficacy of different ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring modalities in this patient population remains unclear. Objective To compare the diagnostic yield and clinical utility of 3 ambulatory electrocardiographic modalities in pediatric patients. Design, Setting, and Participants This single-center study took place at an outpatient clinic and an inpatient ward of National Taiwan University Children’s Hospital. Patients younger than 18 years who underwent ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring between December 2022 and January 2025 were included. These data were analyzed February 2025 to March 2026. Exposure A continuous 7-day Holter device that functioned as an event recorder was used. Recordings from the first 24 hours were defined as the 24-hour Holter results. Main Outcomes and Measures Arrhythmias were categorized as major (tachyarrhythmia or bradyarrhythmia) or minor (extrasystolic arrhythmia). All patients were followed up for 1 year; the final arrhythmia diagnosis was used as the reference standard. The primary and secondary outcomes were detection of arrhythmia and a change in clinical management attributable to monitoring findings, respectively. Results In total, 435 children (235 female [54%] and 200 male [46%]; mean [SD] age, 12.3 [3.9] years) were included. The mean (SD) duration of analyzable ambulatory electrocardiographic data was 4.9 (1.7) days. Of 411 children who activated the event recorder, 10.7% had symptom-correlated arrhythmias. The 7-day Holter monitoring demonstrated a significantly higher rate of major arrhythmias (6.2%) than the 24-hour Holter or 7-day event recordings (2.3%; rate difference 95% CI, 1.9%-6.0%; P &lt; .001). Seven-day Holter monitoring showed superior sensitivity (7-day Holter monitoring: 73%; rate difference 95% CI, 54.1%-84.6%; 24-hour Holter monitoring: 27%; rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; and 7-day event recorder: 27%, rate difference 95% CI, 13.4%-43.1%; P &lt; .001) and a high negative predictive value (97.5%, 95% CI, 95.2%-98.6%). Tachyarrhythmias were associated with higher rates of management changes; management changed in 7.1% of patients with 7-day Holter monitoring, 1.6% with 24-hour Holter (rate difference 95% CI, 3.0%-7.6%; P &lt; .001) and 2.8% with a 7-day event recorder (rate difference 95% CI, 2.0%-6.2%; P &lt; .001). Conclusions and Relevance In this study of pediatric patients without structural heart disease who underwent electrocardiographic monitoring, 7-day continuous ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring was associated with a significantly higher diagnostic yield than 24-hour Holter and 7-day event recording. Continuous monitoring may be preferred to detect tachyarrhythmias likely to influence clinical management.

items.title: Rates of Nicotine Use Among Children and Adolescents
items.abstract: This repeated cross-sectional study evaluates rates of nicotine use among US children and adolescents.

items.title: No Caffeine for Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
Maternal Autoimmune Diseases During Pregnancy and Offspring Type 1 Diabetes
items.abstract: IMPORTANCE Maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy may influence the long-term risk of immune-mediated diseases in offspring, but the relative contributions of prenatal and familial factors to offspring type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain unclear. OBJECTIVE To investigate the association between a broad spectrum of maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy and offspring T1D, and to compare the associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS This population-based cohort study included children identified from national health registers who were born in Sweden between 2001 and 2014, and were followed up from birth until T1D diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from November 2025 to June 2026. EXPOSURE Parental autoimmune diseases diagnosed before or during pregnancy, identified from national health registers. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES The primary outcome was incident T1D in offspring. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs for offspring T1D were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models. Associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases before childbirth with offspring T1D were directly compared, and cousin analyses were performed to assess the potential role of shared familial factors. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 10 273 (0.71%) of the 1 455 645 included individuals (51.4% male and 48.6% female; median [IQR], age 15.3 [11.9-19.0] years) developed T1D. Maternal autoimmune disease during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D (adjusted HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.46-1.68); paternal autoimmune disease before childbirth showed a similar association (adjusted HR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.37-1.67). No overall difference was observed in maternal-paternal comparisons (ratio of HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.92-1.17), but heterogeneity was observed across specific disease categories. A clear gradient in T1D risk was observed according to parental T1D status, with the highest risk among offspring with both parents affected, followed by paternal T1D only and maternal T1D only. In cousin analyses, the association with maternal autoimmune disease was attenuated but persisted (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.08-1.50). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE In this population-based cohort study, maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of offspring T1D. Comparable associations of maternal and paternal autoimmune diseases with offspring T1D suggest a role of shared familial susceptibility, while disease-specific differences indicate that some conditions could have parental-specific effects, suggesting contributions from shared familial susceptibility and potential intrauterine mechanisms.

items.title: What Parents Should Know About Reducing Food Allergy Risk
items.abstract: This JAMA Pediatrics Patient Page describes what can be done to reduce the risk of food allergies in children.

items.title: Prenatal Exposure to Wildfire PM 2.5 and Risk of ASD and ADHD in Children Enrolled in Medicaid
items.abstract: Importance Wildfires are an increasing source of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), yet evidence on prenatal wildfire smoke exposure and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes remains limited. Objective To examine whether prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 is associated with risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a population-based cohort study of the US nationwide Medicaid population using Medicaid Analytic Extract (MAX) data from 2007 to 2014 with follow-up through childhood. Included were mother-child pairs with continuous enrollment and stable residential zip code during pregnancy. Exposure Weekly wildfire smoke–attributable PM 2.5 at 1-km 2 resolution, aggregated to the zip code level across pregnancy. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident ASD and ADHD identified using validated claims-based algorithms. Associations were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards models with distributed lag nonlinear models. Results A total of 893 212 mother-child pairs (mother mean [SD] age, 24.7 [5.9] years) were included in this analysis. Children entered the cohort at birth (452 218 [50.6%] male). Mean (SD) observed follow-up was 6.3 (2.4) years for children diagnosed with ASD and 7.1 (1.9) years for children diagnosed with ADHD. Among 893 212 children, 8357 were diagnosed with ASD and 22 302 with ADHD. The cumulative incidence until age 8 years was 1.9% for ASD and 10.4% for ADHD. An IQR increase in cumulative wildfire PM 2.5 exposure (0.75 µg/m 3 ) during pregnancy was associated with increased risk of ASD (hazard ratio [HR], 1.30; 95% CI, 1.07-1.59) but not ADHD (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.91-1.17). Associations for ASD were strongest during midpregnancy to late gestation compared with early gestation. Results were robust to sensitivity analyses. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this cohort study show that prenatal exposure to wildfire-related PM 2.5 may be associated with increased risk of ASD but not ADHD. These findings highlight the potential neurodevelopmental impacts of wildfire smoke and underscore the need for strategies to reduce exposure during pregnancy as wildfire activity intensifies.
