Individualized Cardiac Index–Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery
items.abstract: Importance It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index. Objective To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. Design, Setting, and Participants This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026. Interventions Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient’s preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Results Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Conclusions and Relevance Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient’s preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279

Childhood Cancer Risk After Assisted Reproductive Technology
items.abstract: Importance Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type. Objective To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type. Design, Setting, and Population Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023. Exposures Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer. Main Outcomes and Measures Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Results During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. Conclusions and Relevance ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest that procedure-related, rather than infertility-related, factors warrant further investigation.

items.title: Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years
items.abstract: Importance Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. Observations Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity ( LEPR , POMC , and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. Conclusions and Relevance Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy
items.abstract: Importance For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. Objective To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. Design, Setting, and Participants From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Interventions Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. Results All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively ( P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. Conclusions and Relevance For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03164473

items.title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation
items.abstract: Importance People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. Objective To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. Design, Setting, and Participants This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks’ gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks’ gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. Results The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

items.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in ERBB2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Importance Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) has demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in a global phase 1 trial involving heavily pretreated patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)–low metastatic breast cancer. Objective To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer. Design, Setting, and Participants This open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial was conducted at 73 hospitals across China. Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]–negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor–positive disease. Enrollment began on June 30, 2023, and ended on August 20, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the final analysis for progression-free survival in the current study was March 20, 2026. Interventions Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician’s choice of chemotherapy (n = 274). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population. Results Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, a total of 551 patients were randomized, with a mean (SD) age of 54.9 (9.9) years. At the data cutoff (March 20, 2026), trastuzumab rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with chemotherapy in the chemotherapy-naive patients (median, 16.6 [95% CI, 14.0-19.4] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-7.0] months; hazard ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.19-0.33]; P &lt; .001) and the overall population (median, 16.4 [95% CI, 14.0-16.8] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-6.9] months; hazard ratio, 0.27 [95% CI, 0.21-0.34]; P &lt; .001). The benefit was consistent in hormone receptor–negative disease (median progression-free survival: 16.5 vs 6.8 months; hazard ratio, 0.34, [95% CI, 0.22-0.54]) and hormone receptor–positive disease (median progression-free survival: 16.4 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.18-0.33]). Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% of patients (232/276) with trastuzumab rezetecan and 67.9% (184/271) with chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (180 [65.2%] vs 147 [54.2%]). Conclusions and Relevance Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05814354

Increased Hemoglobin With Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibitors—A Consistent Extra Benefit?
Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis
items.abstract: Importance In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear. Objective To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator. Data Sources PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026. Study Selection Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Data Extraction and Synthesis Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin). Results A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P &lt; .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and −0.08 g/dL (95% CI, −0.13 to −0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P &lt; .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P &lt; .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and −0.13% (95% CI, −0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P &lt; .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (−2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs −0.10% in control group; difference, −0.84% [95% CI, −1.21% to −0.47%]; P &lt; .001). Conclusions and Relevance In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

items.title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression
items.abstract: Importance Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy- N , N -dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT 1A ) and 5-HT 2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation. Objective To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression. Design, Setting, and Participants Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025. Interventions After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing. Results Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, −11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs −5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, −5.3 [95% CI, −8.9 to −1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, −12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, −6.2 [95% CI, −10.2 to −2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg). Conclusions and Relevance In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05870540

Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function
items.abstract: Importance For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. Objective To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). Design, Setting, and Participants The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Interventions Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. Results The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, −10.1% [95% CI, −16.8% to −3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; −7.9% [95% CI, −13.0% to −2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. Conclusions and Relevance Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921

items.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion
items.abstract: Importance Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. Objective To determine if either reduced-dose non–vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. Design, Setting, and Participants This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. Interventions Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. Results The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, −1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, −3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, −0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria ( P &lt; .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. Conclusions and Relevance Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463

Nonreceipt of Newborn Vitamin K and Risk of Bleeding
items.abstract: Importance Refusal of newborn prophylactic vitamin K has been increasing in the US, placing more infants at risk for vitamin K deficiency bleeding. Objective To describe US trends in nonreceipt of newborn vitamin K and infant bleeding, and to compare risks of bleeding and mortality with concurrent bleeding among infants who did and did not receive newborn intramuscular (IM) vitamin K. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study included infants born at 35 to 43 weeks’ gestation between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, at hospitals and health systems from 50 states contributing to the Epic Cosmos dataset. Exposure Nonreceipt of newborn IM vitamin K. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was bleeding within the first 6 months of life based on International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. Secondary outcomes were bleeding during the birth hospitalization and after discharge, intracranial bleeding, and mortality with concurrent bleeding during the birth hospitalization. Robust Poisson regression was used to estimate relative risks while adjusting for covariates. Results Among 5 240 780 infants, the rate of vitamin K nonreceipt increased from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Between 2017 and 2025, the incidence of bleeding by 6 months increased from 225.3 to 394.0 per 10 000 births in infants who did not receive newborn IM vitamin K, compared with 136.6 to 221.8 per 10 000 in infants who received vitamin K. Infants who did not receive vitamin K had significantly higher risk of bleeding by 6 months than infants who did receive vitamin K (288.0 vs 185.9 per 10 000; adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 1.47; 95% CI, 1.43-1.51). They also had higher risk of intracranial bleeding (33.0 vs 13.2 per 10 000; ARR, 2.43; 95% CI, 2.26-2.62) and mortality with concurrent bleeding during the birth hospitalization (2.9 vs 1.1 per 10 000; ARR, 2.69; 95% CI, 2.09-3.47). Conclusions and Relevance Nonreceipt of vitamin K and infant bleeding incidence have increased in the US, and newborns who did not receive vitamin K were at significantly higher risk of bleeding during their first 6 months.

Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial
items.abstract: Background Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival. Methods In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual. Findings From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative. Interpretation In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer. Funding Bristol Myers Squibb.

items.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial
items.abstract: Background Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone. Methods This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete. Findings Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths. Interpretation The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications. Funding The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development.

Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease. METHODS: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing. FINDINGS: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease. FUNDING: Agios Pharmaceuticals.

Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting. FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns. INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis. FUNDING: Novartis.

items.title: Optimising late-line treatment administration in metastatic colorectal cancer: an even brighter SUNLIGHT

14-day versus 28-day trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan
items.abstract: Background Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival. Methods PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m 2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment. Findings Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group. Interpretation A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. Funding Japan Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI Grant-in-Aid for Challenging Research (Pioneering).

items.title: Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?

Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
items.abstract: Background Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. Methods HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m 2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m 2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing. Findings Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p Interpretation Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting. Funding Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China
items.abstract: Background Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Methods In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116. Findings Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p Interpretation In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population. Funding Baili-Bio (Chengdu) Pharmaceutical.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2– breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Background Patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer have few treatment options. Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class, epidermal growth factor receptor and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate that contains a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (Ed-04). The aim of PANKU-Breast01 was to compare the efficacy and safety of iza-bren versus chemotherapy in patients with pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer. Methods In this randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre study in 72 hospitals in China, patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer who had disease progression after endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg, administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks) or physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, 1·4 mg/m 2 ; vinorelbine, 25 mg/m 2 ; or gemcitabine, 1000 mg/m 2 , all administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks; or capecitabine, 1000-1250 mg/m 2 , administered orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle). Stratified block randomisation was performed by an independent vendor using an interactive web response system, with stratification factors of number of previous lines of chemotherapy, CNS metastasis, and HER2 expression status. Patients, investigators, and site personnel involved in patient care and performing trial procedures were not masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review per RECIST (version 1.1) in the modified intention-to-treat population, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who had at least one dose of study drug. Median progression-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06343948, and is closed to recruitment. Findings Between April 24, 2024, and June 6, 2025, 560 patients were screened, 177 were excluded, and 383 patients were randomly assigned and treated (190 were assigned to the iza-bren group and 193 were assigned to the chemotherapy group). All 383 participants in the study were female and of Chinese ethnicity. Median age was 54·0 years (IQR 47·0-60·0). At data cutoff (July 21, 2026), median follow-up for progression-free survival was 15·2 months (95% CI 13·9-16·8). Iza-bren significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (log-rank p Interpretation Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted. Funding Baili-Bio (Chengdu) Pharmaceutical, CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding, and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

items.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Background Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Methods In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m 2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m 2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to Findings Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p Interpretation Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options. Funding Merck Sharp & Dohme.

items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Background A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Methods The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m 2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing. Findings Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism). Interpretation First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy). Funding Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
items.abstract: Background In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. Methods In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Findings Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I 2 =62·9%; τ 2 =0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I 2 =99·2%; τ 2 =0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I 2 =97·8%; τ 2 =0·156). Interpretation Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. Funding Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut–brain interaction
items.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.
